## 1. What was read

**874 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **259** records (23% of the 1,133 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 496 | 173 | 95 | 334 | 35 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: sysbio +46%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 144, Nature 100, JAMA 98, Science 93, Lancet 56, Bioinformatics 43.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**Single-cell foundation models and the case against them are in the same two
journals in the same month.** Three titles carry explicit single-cell
foundation-model language. [EpiAgent](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40999099/)
is pretrained on a curated human scATAC corpus and encodes chromatin
accessibility as "cell sentences", taking the modality off RNA and handling
annotation, imputation, perturbation-response prediction and zero-shot typing.
*Nature Biotechnology* publishes
[Overcoming barriers to the wide adoption of single-cell large language models](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41131148/),
a Comment reporting that scLLMs remain little used in practice, with technical
gaps and practical barriers standing between the benchmark studies and the bench.
The capability and the adoption gap are stated within weeks of each other by the
same publishing apparatus.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-26"
    An earlier version of this paragraph claimed the vocabulary arrived here
    for the first time, and that skepticism had led it by about three months.
    Neither survives the 2025-01..07 backfill. "Virtual cell" was already in a
    [*Nature Biotechnology* title in April 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40229360/),
    two months before the [*Cell* challenge](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40578317/)
    that named it, and single-cell foundation models were being
    [evaluated as a class in April](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40251685/)
    and [again in June](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40500402/). The
    vocabulary and its critique have been co-present since spring 2025. What is
    true of November is narrower and duller: this is when both reached *Nature
    Methods* and *Nature Biotechnology* together. Every "first appearance" claim
    in this corpus is bounded by which months were searched, and each month's
    reader searched only its own.

**A brain-to-gut circuit, traced end to end.**
[40841473](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40841473/) (*Nature Cancer*) reports
that colorectal cancer cells hijack a polysynaptic circuit running from GABAergic
lateral septum neurons to enteric cholinergic neurons to sustain tumour growth,
and that chronic restraint stress potentiates it. A named anatomical route, the
transmitter systems at both ends, and a behavioural modifier, in one paper.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph said two independent groups had described the same circuit in
    the same issue, citing 40841473 and
    [41057693](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41057693/) together, and called
    convergence in one issue "the strongest evidence grade available from
    literature alone" — the argument that was supposed to separate this thread
    from the checkpoint thread, where nominations never recur.

    41057693 is the *Nature Cancer* News & Views on 40841473. There is one study
    here, and its own journal's write-up of it. The thread may still be the
    healthiest in the file, but this is not the reason: an echo counted as
    convergence is a worse error than a wrong stance, because a wrong stance
    argues and an echo only agrees with itself.

**PD-1's own logic was questioned.**
[41299179](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41299179/) (*Nature*, indexed 2026-01)
reports that the inhibitory PD-1 axis maintains high-avidity stem-like CD8 T
cells. If sustained PD-1 signalling preserves the pool that checkpoint blockade
depends on, then permanent blockade and the entire next-generation-checkpoint
design premise need restating.

**CAR-T's growth edge is autoimmunity, not solid tumours.** Anti-BCMA CAR-T in
[progressive multiple sclerosis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41101309/) and
dual CD19/BCMA co-infusion in
[refractory lupus](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40993243/) are single-arm and
small, but the direction is unambiguous and it is why `car-t-solid` was merged
into `cell-therapy` — the narrower claim could no longer hold the evidence.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41023479](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41023479/) (*Nat Immunol*):
plasmacytoid dendritic cells are dispensable or detrimental in viral infection.
[41191775](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41191775/) (*Sci Transl Med*):
depleting pDCs rescues HIV-reactive stem-like CD8 T cells. The therapeutic
direction on a cell type treated for twenty years as a protective interferon
source is removal.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    [41136761](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41136761/), "A co-stimulatory
    signal via the coinhibitory TIGIT", was listed here as a fresh inversion, on
    the reading that the receptor's assigned sign had been reversed *again*, two
    months after [41094201](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41094201/) and in the
    same journal.

    It was not two months and it was not again. 41136761 is the *Nature
    Immunology* front-matter piece accompanying 41094201 in the same issue, and
    PubMed carries no abstract for it. Both were carded `refutes` on both of the
    same two threads. One observation about TIGIT — that a receptor classified as
    co-inhibitory and pursued as a blockade target carries a tissue-protective
    function — was counted twice, and the sentence manufactured a recurrence out
    of the duplication. The observation stands; it is 41094201's.

[40924026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40924026/) (*JEM*): gut regulatory T
cells are *required* for host disease tolerance in Salmonella superspreaders.

[40742298](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40742298/) (*Cancer Discov*): sucralose
consumption ablates immunotherapy response through microbiome disruption. Filed
as a refutation on the neuro-immune-microbiome thread, because it removes the
assumption that diet is a neutral background in checkpoint trials. If the effect
size transfers to humans at dietary doses, it is an uncontrolled variable in
every trial the corpus tracks.

### (b) Method credibility

Ten cards, the largest month. Two on genome editing:
[HDR-enhancing DNA-PKcs inhibition causes large-scale genomic alterations](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39604565/)
and [repair of double-strand breaks leaves heritable impairment to genome function](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41196998/).
The second is the more serious: it says the damage survives successful repair,
which no editing platform's safety case currently accounts for.

[39592777](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39592777/) (*Nat Biotechnol*): standard
single-cell batch integration destroys real biological signal. The correction
class over-corrects, and every atlas built through it inherits the loss.

[40930103](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40930103/) (*Cell Genomics*): analog
epigenetic memory revealed by targeted chromatin editing — DNA methylation holds
gene expression at analog levels over time rather than switching it binary.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This entry read as "two independent papers overturning the same binary", the
    second being
    [41232507](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41232507/), "The dimmer switch in
    epigenetics". That record is the *Cell Genomics* preview of 40930103 in the
    same issue; its whole abstract is one sentence pointing at it. The binary is
    overturned once, by the paper that did the chromatin editing.

[41193809](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41193809/) (*Nature*, indexed 2026-01):
specificity, length and luck drive gene rankings in association studies.

Retractions: [sFRP2 in the aged microenvironment](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41162716/)
as a driver of melanoma metastasis and therapy resistance, and
[sponges at the root of the animal tree](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41232001/).
